What is Goddess Pose?

Goddess Pose, commonly called Utkata Konasana, is a wide-legged standing squat. The feet turn outward, the knees bend in line with the toes, and the torso stays upright. It develops leg strength, stability, and body awareness.

How do I do Goddess Pose?

Stand with your feet wide and turn your toes outward. Bend your knees while keeping them aligned with the direction of your toes. Lower your hips only as far as comfortable, keep your chest upright, and keep your spine neutral. You can bring your hands to your chest or extend your arms comfortably. Breathe steadily while holding the pose, then straighten your legs slowly to release.

What is Downward-Facing Dog?

Downward-Facing Dog, or Adho Mukha Svanasana, is an inverted V-shaped yoga posture. The hands and feet support the body while the hips move up and back. It is commonly used to lengthen the body and strengthen the arms and legs.

How do I do Downward Dog?

Start on your hands and knees. Spread your fingers and place your hands around shoulder-width apart. Tuck your toes and lift your knees, sending your hips up and back. Lengthen your spine and keep your knees slightly bent if needed. Press through your hands and keep your head relaxed. Breathe steadily, then lower your knees to release.

How do I do Warrior II?

Stand in a wide stance facing the long side of your mat. Turn one foot outward and angle the back foot slightly inward. Bend the front knee while keeping it aligned over the ankle. Extend both arms at shoulder height in opposite directions. Keep your torso upright and shoulders relaxed. Gaze toward the front hand if comfortable. Hold for several steady breaths, then straighten the front leg and repeat on the other side.

Press firmly through your hands, keep your legs active, and gently engage your abdomen. Keep breathing steadily. Lower your knees or return to a comfortable position to release.

What is Tree Pose?

Tree Pose, or Vrksasana, is a standing balance posture. You stand on one leg while the other foot rests on the inner standing leg, above or below the knee. It develops balance, concentration, and lower-body stability.

How do I do Tree Pose?

Begin standing upright with both feet grounded. Shift your weight onto one leg. Place the other foot against the inner standing leg, either above or below the knee, but not directly on the knee. Keep your pelvis level and look at a steady point ahead. Bring your hands to your chest or raise them overhead if comfortable. Hold for several breaths, then lower the foot and switch sides.
